html:
The Durand Line is the border between Afghanistan and Pakistan, about 2,600 kilometres long, agreed in Kabul on 12 November 1893 between the British diplomat Mortimer Durand and the Afghan emir Abdur Rahman Khan.

It marked the limit of British India's influence. The line cut through the lands of the Pashtun tribes, leaving millions on the British side, in what became Pakistan's Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and tribal areas, while the Pashtun-led Afghan state lay to the west.

No Afghan government has formally accepted it as an international border since Pakistan was born in 1947. The dispute soured relations from the start. In the Soviet war and after, fighters, refugees and smugglers crossed it freely, and the Taliban used the tribal belt as a base. Pakistan has since fenced most of it.
sum: The Durand Line is the border between Afghanistan and Pakistan, about 2,600 kilometres long, agreed in Kabul on 12 November 1893 between the British diplomat Mortimer Durand and the Afghan emir Abdur Rahman Khan.
